question: By means of an amendment to the 2024 Regional Stability Law, which became Article 25 of Regional Law No 4 of 25 January 2024, Abruzzo Regional Council reduced the area of the Borsacchio regional reserve in the municipality of Roseto dei Abruzzi (Province of Teramo) from some 1 140 hectares to just 24.7 hectares, thus taking protection away from 98 % of the area.

Article 22 (1) of Law No 394 of 6/12/1991 provides for the participation of provinces, mountain communities and municipalities in the process of establishing protected areas, by dint of conferences to draw up the guidance document on the territorial analysis of the area to protect, its provisional perimeter, the setting of objectives to be pursued and the assessment of the regional effects of the establishing a particular protected area.

That procedure was not followed. From a nature perspective, the area of the Borsacchio regional reserve is extremely important to the region as a whole because it has extraordinary environmental matrices that are significant within the EU framework for conservation interest. The relevant Natura 2000 codes are 1210, 1410, 2110, 2130, 2230 and 2270. Can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Will it check whether Article 5(1) of Directive 92/43/EEC can be applied to the Borsacchio reserve?
Does it take the view that that the Abruzzo Region has infringed Articles 3, 4, 10, 11, 12 and 13 of Directive 92/43/EEC?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.4.2024) 1. Under Directive 92/43/EEC1, Member States select the most important sites for each of the habitat types and species listed in the Annexes I and II of the Directive that are present on their territory, using the scientific criteria laid down in Annex III of the Directive. Then they submit the lists of proposed Sites of Community Importance to the Commission.

Based on these national lists, the Commission identifies the Sites of Community Importance, which become part of the Natura 2000 network, and formally adopts their lists for each European biogeographic region2.

The Borsacchio regional reserve is a protected area established entirely under national and regional legislation and is not part of the Natura 2000 network, nor has it been identified as a site that would require a designation under Directive 92/43/EEC.

As the Commission is not in possession of scientific information on the basis of which it can consider that site essential for the maintenance of priority natural habitat types or for the survival of priority species, it cannot establish whether Article 5 of that Directive may apply.

However, the Commission recalls that the EU Biodiversity Strategy3 aims at protecting a minimum of 30% of the EU’s land area and 30% of the EU’s sea area and at integrating ecological corridors. This political commitment is to be achieved through a combination of the Natura 2000 network and areas designated under national or regional law4. 2.
On the basis of the information provided, no infringement of Articles 3, 4, 10, 11, 12 and 13 of Directive 92/43/EEC could be established.
1 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and

flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50. 2 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/nature-and-biodiversity/natura-2000/designating-natura-2000sites_en#list-of-sites-per-eu-biogeographical-region 3 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/strategy/biodiversity-strategy-2030_en 4 Commission Staff Working Document, Criteria and guidance for protected areas designations, SWD(2022) 23 final.
